summary: gp3 field double-assignment mixes profit rate and monetary amount
detail: Line 78 sets req.body.gp3 = parseFloat(pv.gp3_profit_rate) (a percentage rate like 0.15). Line 82 then sets req.body.gp3 again to parseFloat(pv.gp3_amount) (a monetary value). Since line 78 always assigns a number, line 82's condition !req.body.gp3 is only true when gp3_profit_rate is exactly 0, causing gp3 column to store a monetary amount instead of a rate — type inconsistency.
fix: Remove line 82 entirely. The gp3 column stores the GP3 profit rate, correctly sourced from pv.gp3_profit_rate on line 78. gp3_amount is handled separately on line 83.

summary: Cost-type approval never updates delivery_projects cost_status on completion
detail: Approval creation (line 39) sets cost_status = 'pending'. But the approval record handler (lines 177-190) only handles plan type for delivery_id. The cost type has no corresponding block, so cost_status remains 'pending' permanently.
fix: Add after line 190: if (ar.approval_type === 'cost' && ar.delivery_id) { await query('UPDATE delivery_projects SET cost_status = $1, updated_at = now() WHERE id = $2', [newStatus, ar.delivery_id]); }

summary: Promote locking side effect runs outside transaction — no rollback if POST fails
detail: Lines 46-51 set promote_locked = true BEFORE the actual approval POST handler (crudRoutes) runs. If the INSERT fails, the opportunity stays locked with no approval request created. The lock and insert are in separate auto-commit queries.
fix: Move the lock/unlock logic into the POST handler's response, or use a transaction in the POST middleware passing a flag to roll back on error, or defer the locking to the record creation callback.

summary: Outer catch silently swallows errors and continues to next()
detail: The outer catch block (lines 92-94) catches errors from the side-effect logic (locking, auto-fill), logs them as '锁定机会失败', then falls through to next() on line 95. The middleware continues and the approval is created even if the locking failed or the auto-fill errored. The message on line 93 is also misleading for non-promote type errors.
fix: For critical failures (locking), do not silently continue. Separate the side effects: allow locking errors to propagate via next(err) so they are not silently swallowed.

summary: Duplicate objKeysToSnake call — body and snakeBody both computed from req.body
detail: Line 183: const body = objKeysToSnake({...req.body}) used only for the lock toggle check (line 185). Line 193: snakeBody = objKeysToSnake({...req.body}) recomputed identically for the update. body is redundant after the lock check.
fix: Remove line 183 and the isOnlyLockToggle logic (lines 184-191) into a standalone check using snakeBody from line 193, eliminating the duplicate conversion.

summary: Custom PUT handler duplicates crudRoutes update logic without calling serializeParams
detail: The custom PUT handler (lines 193-206) manually constructs the UPDATE SQL, duplicating helpers.ts lines 131-148. It does NOT call serializeParams, so if any update value contains a JSONB array or special type, it would be passed to pg incorrectly. The custom handler uses RETURNING * while crudRoutes uses quotedFields, creating a response shape inconsistency.
fix: Replace the custom SQL construction with a call to the underlying crudRoutes PUT logic, or add serializeParams call and use quotedFields equivalent for consistency.

summary: Uses req.body.id instead of the converted body
detail: Line 113: const groupId = req.body.id || undefined; — but line 103 already converted body via objKeysToSnake as 'const body = ...'. Should use body.id for consistency. While 'id' has no case difference, this pattern is brittle if any other camelCase field is accessed on req.body directly.
fix: Change to: const groupId = body.id || undefined;

summary: rp1_profit_rate is in ProjectVersionRow type but missing from upsert INSERT/UPDATE
detail: ProjectVersionRow (types.ts line 94) defines rp1_profit_rate: number, but the INSERT on line 58-63 and the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on lines 64-84 do not include rp1_profit_rate. If the DB column is NOT NULL with no default, the INSERT would fail.
fix: Add rp1_profit_rate to both the INSERT column list (lines 58-63) and the ON CONFLICT UPDATE SET clause (lines 64-84), with a default of 0 in the destructuring on line 45-51.

summary: Custom LIST sorts by project_name DESC — unusual sort direction for a name field
detail: The custom LIST (line 36) uses ORDER BY dp.project_name DESC. Typically name fields are sorted ASC for predictable ordering. The crudRoutes standard uses updated_at DESC, so the custom route overrides this with a likely unintentional DESC.
fix: Change to ORDER BY dp.project_name ASC or match the crudRoutes orderBy: 'updated_at DESC'.

summary: serializeParams array type detection heuristic is fragile for mixed-type arrays
detail: The function checks typeof v[0] to decide if an array should be JSON-stringified. Arrays starting with a non-string (number, object, boolean) get stringified; arrays starting with a string are passed as-is. This heuristic fails for mixed-type arrays like [1, 'hello'] — stringified for JSONB but wrong for TEXT[] columns, or ['hello', 1] — passed as-is but wrong for JSONB. Currently works because usage patterns are consistent, but is fragile.
fix: The column type metadata (JSONB vs TEXT[]) should drive the decision, not the first element type. Either pass column-type hints or use separate serialize/deserialize per column.

summary: Three correlated subqueries per row in opportunity list
detail: Lines 69, 71, 73 each run a correlated subquery for every row returned: EXISTS(quotations), quotation amount, and tax_rate via JOIN quotations+project_versions. For a list of 200 opportunities, this runs 600 subqueries. The tax_rate subquery joins two tables per row, making it the most expensive.
fix: Replace the three subqueries with LEFT JOINs to a subquery or CTE that fetches quotation data once. For example: LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT ... FROM quotations q LEFT JOIN project_versions pv ON ... WHERE q.id = so.quotation_id) qdata ON true

summary: Correlated subquery for nodes array in delivery list
detail: Line 23-28: (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(dn_sub) ...) FROM delivery_nodes dn_sub WHERE dn_sub.delivery_project_id = dp.id) runs for every row. For 100 delivery projects, this is 100 separate subquery executions.
fix: Use a LEFT JOIN LATERAL or fetch nodes separately and map in memory after the query, similar to how projects.ts /:id/full does it.

summary: Correlated subquery for latest_record in approval list
detail: Line 112: (SELECT row_to_json(ar2.*) FROM approval_records ar2 WHERE ar2.approval_request_id = ar.id ORDER BY ar2.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) runs for every row in the approval list.
fix: Use a LEFT JOIN LATERAL or fetch latest approval records in a separate batch query and merge in memory.

summary: Four sequential queries in /:id/full instead of JOINs
detail: The handler runs four separate DB round-trips: (1) SELECT from projects, (2) SELECT from project_versions, (3) SELECT from project_groups, (4) SELECT from group_items. Each query is a full round-trip.
fix: Combine (3) and (4) into a single query with LEFT JOIN, or use a batch fetch for items across all groups in one round-trip (already done with ANY($1::uuid[]), but the groups query itself is separate). Consider combining versions query with the project query.

summary: PostgreSQL error detection relies on fragile duck-typing
detail: Line 32-33: const pgErr = err as any; if (pgErr.code && pgErr.severity) — This duck-types to detect PG errors. While this works, it could match non-PG errors that happen to have code and severity properties. Also, the handler does not log the stack trace for PG errors, making debugging harder.
fix: Use a more robust check: check pgErr.code matching the PostgreSQL error code pattern (e.g., pgErr.code && typeof pgErr.code === 'string' && pgErr.code.length === 5). Also log the stack trace in development mode.

summary: POST /notifications allows any authenticated user to create notifications for any user
detail: Lines 304-312: The POST /notifications endpoint accepts user_id from the request body and creates a notification for that user. There is no check that the requesting user matches user_id or has admin role. Any authenticated user can create notifications for any other user.
fix: Add authorization: either restrict to the current user's own notifications (req.user.userId === body.user_id) or require admin/director role.

summary: Auto-created profile with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING never updates stale roles
detail: Line 34-42: The profile is created only if it does not exist (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). If a user's role changes in the main users table, the timerecording profile role becomes stale. There is no mechanism to re-sync.
fix: Use ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET role = EXCLUDED.role, name = EXCLUDED.name to keep the profile in sync with the users table.
